title: Babies learn by mouthing, so coins, batteries, and whole grapes are choking hazards
summary: UNICEF says children explore by putting things in their mouths, which is why small foods, toys, batteries, and coins can block the airway.
body: UNICEF's babyproofing page says children explore by putting things in their mouths, which puts them at risk of choking on food, toys, or small objects. It says to avoid giving young children small hard foods such as nuts, whole grapes, or hard candies, and to keep small toys, batteries, and coins out of reach. Cords and soft bedding are listed beside that as suffocation and strangulation risks. The US infant choking article's treatment steps are not restated. The first-aid cards for a choking baby and a choking child are the place for what to do after an object is stuck. This card is only why small objects matter before that happens.
